title: Value doesn't make sense for the gamble
text:
Okay, the box I received was a pretty good match. I got the single cat box because I wasn't sure how I'd feel about the contents for a house of two kitties, and honestly, that was totally fine. It's not like we go through a bag of treats in a month or toys are like, color-coded per cat. The "College" themed box included a bag of treats, a catnip "textbook" toy, a kicker stick that looks like a brick library building, two hard bouncy "atom" balls, and a pom-pom ended toy that has a bungee cord so if the cat pulls hard enough at the pom-pom treats you've loaded inside will drop. The last had a velcro loop on top so you could hang it, and it says it's adjustable as to how hard they have to pull if your cats dig it.
For my cats, the catnip book has been a hit, the building toy was meh, the atom balls are amusing but they're hard rubber so they won't pick them up and we'll see if they play soccer with them. The pom-pom toy was amusing as a dancer toy, but they haven't pulled hard enough to release treats from it yet. It's a short tube with a short line to the pom-pom so it's not a great dancer toy. Only one of my cats will eat the treats.
That's 2.5 - 3 out of 5 successes for my house. There's no customization, so I figured it wouldn't be all wins, and there was a variety of types of toy which is great. However, according to their math on the insert, the value of the items adds up to $25. If the subscriber price for the box is $20 and not everything tickles your fancy, you might as well just go to PetCo. Having a curated theme and a box that is a nice nap spot doesn't feel like it adds a whole lot of value.
